gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the missing positive factor h−δ^μ in the Shape-Lemma0 increment, including the flat or decreasing cases and the resulting failure of strict increase and derivative claims.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The Shape-Lemma0 formula does not support strict monotonicity under the stated parameter regime because its increment is h−δ^μ; equality gives flat intervals and δ^μ>h reverses the behavior.

component_coverage.gold_component: Missing h−δ^μ factor invalidates strict increase, derivative-zero characterization, and associated bounds under allowed parameters.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 explicitly computes the increment as h−δ^μ, gives the equality and greater-than cases, and proposes the strict condition 0<δ^μ<h.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that φ(t+h)=φ(t)+h does not imply the unit-shift identity unless Jh=1, so the normalization denominator and downstream formulas fail for J=ceil(1/h) on general meshes.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The construction assumes an integral-grid relation Jh=1 that is not imposed by J=ceil(1/h), invalidating the unit-shift normalization, endpoint formulas, and associated estimates.

component_coverage.gold_component: The unit-shift normalization and downstream formulas are unjustified for the general definition J=ceil(1/h), which does not ensure Jh=1.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 states the actual h-shift law, identifies the missing Jh=1 condition, and connects it to disagreement of the ψ definitions, normalization, boundary formulas, and rates.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both give an explicit within-level collision despite rationally independent normalized weights, caused by irrational nodal values and failure of rational-independence reasoning for the encoded centers.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Rational independence of the weights alone does not guarantee distinct encoded centers when the sampled inner-function values are not rational; distinct centers can produce equal scalar abscissae.

component_coverage.gold_component: The rational-independence hypothesis does not prevent within-level encoded-center collisions because the coefficients need not be rational.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 supplies a concrete rationally independent weight choice and equal encoded centers arising from irrational nodal values, and proposes finite collision-hyperplane avoidance as the repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify overlapping row image intervals that prescribe incompatible values, so the row-dependent construction does not define a single-valued global C² outer function.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The row-indexed outer assignments are incompatible on overlapping scalar image intervals; hence no single univariate outer function satisfying all row prescriptions is constructed for the general weight regime.

component_coverage.gold_component: Interlacing or overlapping row images make row-dependent outer assignments inconsistent and prevent construction of a single global outer function.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-011 gives an explicit overlapping-interval example with incompatible row values and concludes that no single-valued g_q can satisfy both prescriptions.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the invalid inference from nearest scalar image to nearby spatial center: scalar proximity does not control preimage distance, producing an unavoidable 1/N error and invalidating the claimed refinement rate.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Choosing a center by minimizing scalar encoded-image distance does not ensure spatial closeness of the preimage, so the gap-level Hölder estimate and pure h^α refinement rate fail.

component_coverage.gold_component: Scalar-image nearest-center selection does not control spatial distance, causing the gap estimate to fail and leaving an O(1/N) error floor.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-013 explicitly constructs a point whose scalar image matches a distant encoded center, derives an error of 1/N, and states that the claimed J-refinement estimate fails.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the interior tangent pole in the d≥3 test target, which makes the exponential expression discontinuous or undefined and invalidates the claimed continuous Hölder experiment.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The eg2D3D4D target uses tan(x₂+⋯+x_d), which has an interior pole on the cube; the resulting exponential has incompatible one-sided behavior and is not a valid continuous test target.

component_coverage.gold_component: The tangent-based high-dimensional test target is undefined and non-continuous on an interior pole, so it cannot instantiate the theorem's continuous Hölder class.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-014 identifies the interior pole, explains the divergent one-sided behavior, and proposes replacing the tangent factor and rerunning the experiments.
